Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **A Text Effects demo**: a ninth demo shows, a page each, what a message window does with its text: colour, size, weight and slant, another font, outlines and shadows, gradients, ruby, pictures in a line, alignment and spacing, indents, speed and pauses, moving text, names, the glossary, a window style and vertical text (in English and Japanese)
- **Characters that move**: `[font anim=shake|wave|pulse|rainbow]` keeps text moving while it shows, and `[font appear=fade|rise|drop|slide]` brings each character in as it's drawn; Reduce Motion holds them still
- **Vertical text works on the SDL engines**: the characters, their ruby, `[hch]` and the punctuation (、。 at the top right, brackets and dashes turned) are where vertical Japanese has them; before, a vertical window drew arrows on top of one another
- **Fixed**: the window's buttons showed over the Effects demo's TV static, which now covers them as it covers the window; a `[style]` before a line's text was lost in a line mode; a 。 after an `[emb]` could start a line in Japanese; a script-drawn transition of the whole page showed the message window black; a compiled scene's title in the corner was always in the source language
- **The Character demo's flashback fades in and out**: it jumped into place and, at its end, went black and faded in from black. `[env restore]` with a transition now crossfades from the scene on the screen to the kept one, and a message window style set behind a global transition changes with it
- kagex-release 0.23.0 downloads the 0.23.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.23.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
